components.title: The Water Cycle
components.subtitle: How water moves through air, land, and sea

components.text: Evaporation is the process by which liquid water turns into water vapour. The Sun heats water in oceans, lakes, and rivers, and the fastest-moving molecules escape into the air as a gas. Plants also release water vapour through their leaves, a process called transpiration.

As water vapour rises, it cools. Cooler air holds less vapour, so the vapour changes back into tiny liquid droplets. These droplets gather around dust particles and form clouds, which is why clouds appear high in the sky.

When the droplets in a cloud grow large and heavy, they fall to the ground as rain, snow, sleet, or hail. Precipitation returns water to lakes, rivers, and oceans, and it soaks into the soil, where it can be taken up by plants or flow underground.
Worked example: a puddle after rain
Follow one puddle from a rainy afternoon to a dry sidewalk the next morning.

items.label: Rain
items.text: Rain falls and collects in a low spot on the sidewalk, forming a puddle.

items.label: Evaporation
items.text: Warm sunlight heats the puddle, and water molecules at the surface escape as vapour.

items.label: Condensation
items.text: The vapour rises, cools, and forms droplets that become part of a cloud.

items.label: Precipitation
items.text: Later, those droplets may fall again as rain, completing the cycle.

questions.question: What process turns liquid water into water vapour?
questions.explanation: Evaporation is the change from liquid to vapour, driven mainly by heat from the Sun.

questions.question: Why do clouds form as vapour rises?
options: The vapour heats up and expands
The vapour cools and condenses into droplets
The vapour freezes into ice crystals at ground level
The vapour is pulled into the soil
questions.explanation: Cooler air holds less vapour, so the vapour condenses into tiny droplets around dust particles.

questions.question: Which of these is an example of precipitation?
questions.explanation: Precipitation is water falling from clouds as rain, snow, sleet, or hail.
